Mini Sudoku on NoCharge: A Quiet 6×6

A source-checked look at NoCharge Mini Sudoku’s fixed six-by-six board, three-by-two boxes, number pad, and session-only state.

By NoCharge Editorial·Reviewed by NoCharge Editorial·Published August 23, 2026·Updated November 24, 2026·2 min read
Try the detail in a live board.

A small grid, a quiet puzzle.

Play Mini Sudoku 6×6Browse all Articles

Bottom line: Mini Sudoku is a six-by-six Sudoku with digits 1–6 and three-by-two boxes. The current V2 game uses a fixed puzzle and answer, a number pad, and no saved progress or difficulty selector.

Six rows, six columns, three-by-two boxes

Each digit must appear once in every row, column, and 3×2 box. Given cells are locked. Select an empty cell and choose a digit from the on-screen number pad; Clear cell removes an entry. The game does not provide pencil marks, a reveal button, or a difficulty menu.

What the checks mean

The engine rejects a digit that repeats in the current row, column, or box. It also compares a non-repeating entry with the bundled solution and increments the visible Checks counter when the entry differs. A mistake does not end the puzzle; the counter is feedback, not a score or a grade.

Fixed board, no saved record

The current source initializes the same six-by-six puzzle and solution on reset. It is not a runtime puzzle generator and does not offer a saved board that resumes after reload. The grid and number-pad buttons are standard controls; use the current game page for its complete interaction details.

A smaller board can feel less visually dense than a nine-by-nine grid, but that is a layout difference—not a promise about difficulty, solving time, or cognitive benefit.
